newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Panonska bank stock almost sold out.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Panonska bank stock almost sold out.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Panonska banka has almost sold out its entire four million dinar issue of ordinary shares listed earlier this month on the Belgrade bourse, the Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Monday.
According to the bourse report, Panonska sold 7,992 out of 8,000 individual shares worth 3.995 million dinars. All shares had a 500 dinar face value.
Shares were sold through the brokerage house Trziste Novca.

"This has only been a primary sale of part of the bank's issue. For the time being, we cannot reveal the investors' identity. And it is up to an issuer to say who bought its shares," said Trziste Novca official who asked not to be named.
The remaining eight shares unsold will be on offer until an investor is found, the source said.
There was no one at the bank immediately available for comment.

The Yugoslav Securities Commission, in an attempt to enable development of the local financial market, decided late last year to launch a regulation under which a share issue is considered successful only if the entire issue is sold out, part of it on the bourse.
Panonska banka, along with AIK banka and Kulska banka, listed shares on the BSE two weeks ago but did not immediately find buyers for its stock.
But the source insisted it had nothing to do with investor interest.

"There is a difference between a small and a medium size bank. In small banks, any decision on new shareholders lies with the general manager, but in a larger bank, it is the board of directors who decide, so it takes more time," the source said.
This was the only reason why Panonska needed the whole week to sell its stake listed on the bourse, the source said. "Otherwise, Panonska stock is an attractive investment," the source said.
